Travel & Rewards

Points, status and card perks that fit how you travel

Loyalty programs and credit card perks can be worth real money, but only when they match how you actually travel. These guides explain how airline and hotel programs award status, what elite benefits do and don't cover, and how to route everyday spending to the right card.

If you plan to travel more as work winds down, the case studies show how program rules played out on real trips, including what happened when plans went wrong.

Common questions

Which airline program fits my home airport?

Status is most useful with the airline that flies the most routes from where you live. The airline guides compare how each program earns and spends miles and which cities each one serves best.

  • Airline Loyalty Programs Compared
  • United MileagePlus Guide 2027
  • American AAdvantage Guide
  • Delta SkyMiles Guide

Is chasing status worth it?

Compare what you would spend to earn status with the benefits you would actually use, such as upgrades, free checked bags and same-day changes.

  • Is Airline Status Worth It? Status Value vs Cost Calculator
  • The Delay Text on the Way to BWI

Which hotel program should I focus on?

Pick the chain with hotels where you travel most, then compare how quickly each program's nights and points turn into free stays.

  • Hotel Loyalty Programs Compared
  • Marriott Bonvoy Guide
  • Hilton Honors Guide
  • World of Hyatt Guide
  • IHG One Rewards Guide

Which card should I use for each purchase?

The best card depends on the category of spending and on the protections you need, not only on the points rate.

  • Card Rewards Router
  • The $2,400 Mountain Blizzard
  • The $3,200 Basic Economy Gamble

How do I pay less for the trip itself?

Flexible dates, the right booking channel and memberships you already hold often matter more than points.
